A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SCOPE research work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison. Appendices A–D are retained, and v3 adds Appendix E.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark results in Table 1, ablations in Table 2, sensitivity and training analyses in Figures 3–5, and generated solutions in Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains the original experiments and appendix case study and adds pseudo-label accuracy results in Section 5.4 and Table 3.

M1.justification: The confidence-weighted voting, bootstrap label estimation, subgroup partitioning, Pareto size selection, and GRPO update remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 is retained. The segmentation disclosure and corrections distinguishing responses from extracted answers do not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate mathematical reasoning on AIME 2024, AIME 2025, AMC, and MATH-500, with the same dataset examples and sizes in Appendix B. The added pseudo-label diagnostic does not identify an additional dataset, domain, or test scenario.

E2.justification: The model-specific comparator rows in Table 1 are unchanged, including TTRL, INTUITOR, RLPR, CO-REWARDING-I, and EVOL-RL. Existing ablation and figure comparisons are retained. New Table 3 reuses TTRL and the previously studied fixed-subgroup variants.

E3.justification: Section 5.4 introduces pseudo-label accuracy, measuring agreement between training-time consensus labels and ground truth, using Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B. This adds a diagnostic evaluation protocol; the existing model configurations and Appendix C training and pass@1 evaluation settings remain unchanged. The new diagnostic's dataset and aggregation procedure are unspecified.

E4.justification: New Section 5.4 and Table 3 examine whether subgroup partitioning reduces consensus drift, comparing pseudo-label accuracy for TTRL, fixed sizes 1, 8, and 64, and automatic SCOPE. This is a focused addition to the retained component ablations, parameter sensitivity, confidence-granularity analysis, training curves, and appendix case study.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains the same uncertainty entries and reporting format. Neither version specifies training-run counts or seeds or explains those uncertainty entries. v3 adds no confidence intervals, significance tests, or statistical estimation procedure; Table 3 reports point values.

E6.justification: New Table 3 reports pseudo-label accuracy of 25.42 for TTRL, 26.75/26.84/29.57 for fixed subgroup sizes 1/8/64, and 30.71 for automatic SCOPE, a reported 20.81% relative improvement over TTRL. Existing Tables 1–2, Figures 3–5, and appendix solutions are unchanged. Section 4.2 changes the stated average-score margin from 4.40 to 4.41, while Table 1 still displays 4.40.

T1.justification: Equations 9–10 correct the formal distinction between a response and its extracted answer: Equation 9 compares Ans(o) directly with the consensus label, and Equation 10 applies Ans to each response before comparison. These repair the written reward and quality-rate definitions to agree with Equation 7. No new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central contributions and claims: step-wise confidence and adaptive subgroups mitigate confirmation bias and sparse rewards and improve reasoning performance. The headline AIME 2025 and AMC gains are unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 5.4 newly interprets higher pseudo-label accuracy across fixed and automatic subgroup settings as evidence of reduced consensus drift and improved label stability. The existing interpretations of quality–diversity trade-offs and the limitations concerning heuristic segmentation and approximately 10% computational overhead remain.

D1.justification: Section 3.1 now specifies two consecutive newline characters as the reasoning-step delimiter; v1 mentioned newline-based segmentation only more generally in Limitations. This improves implementation disclosure without establishing a setting change. Appendix C hyperparameters, prompts, sampling settings, model checkpoints, and code access information are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Huang et al. (2026) on stepwise adaptive thinking and Xu et al. (2026) on multi-token policy optimization. The introduction distinguishes reward reliability from reasoning-efficiency work, and Related Work adds action-space granularity as context. The broader positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 makes distributed grammar and terminology edits and shortens portions of the results discussion and appendix case-study explanation. It adds Section 5.4, acknowledgments, and Appendix E on AI-assisted translation and polishing. The overall narrative and section sequence remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Table 3, corrects Figure 2's 'Meta-Group' terminology to 'Subgroup' and panel label (g) to (f), and renumbers the appendix tables. Content shifts across pages and page-number footers disappear. The existing performance plots and appendix solution figures are retained.

improvement.justification: The new pseudo-label accuracy comparison provides direct, limited evidence about label reliability beyond v1's downstream accuracy and training curves. The exact segmentation disclosure and corrected answer-comparison equations also improve clarity. These are modest gains: the new diagnostic leaves its dataset, aggregation, and uncertainty unspecified, limiting how strongly it establishes reduced consensus drift.
